Mandel would (a) replace any KFold/TimeSeriesSplit in the repo with PurgedKFold using an embargo at least as long as a market's resolution lag, because prediction-market labels resolve days after the trade and unpurged folds leak the outcome; (b) emit CPCV backtest paths so the gate reports a distribution of Sharpe ratios rather than one number; (c) call the DSR and PBO functions directly as the acceptance test. It is small (57 stars, 141 commits, CI and PyPI release), so pin a version, vendor its tests, and verify its formulas against the two Bailey/Lopez de Prado PDFs above before trusting it. Alternatives with CombinatorialPurgedCV: skfolio (https://skfolio.org/generated/skfolio.model_selection.CombinatorialPurgedCV.html).

candidates.title: Arbitrage Analysis in Polymarket NBA Markets (Cheng, Yang, Zou; arXiv 2605.00864, Apr 2026)
candidates.one_line: Reconstructs continuous market state from 75M+ limit-order-book snapshots across 173 NBA games; single-market mispricings were nearly nonexistent in-game (7 executable episodes, median life 3.6 s), combinatorial episodes were more common (290, clustered in the final minutes) with a median return of 101 bp, but 76.9% could be filled only at an average size of 14.8 shares, confining risk-free extraction to retail scale.
candidates.what_it_adds: Supplies the parameters for a realistic execution model, which the repo currently has no evidence for: opportunity half-life measured in seconds, depth-limited fill sizes, and the finding that shallow books, not detection, are the bottleneck. Mandel's backtest harness should fill against snapshot depth rather than mid-price and should reject any child strategy whose edge vanishes when a 3 s latency or a ~15-share size cap is imposed; those two stress tests belong in the validation gate as hard requirements. I confirmed the abstract page and the numbers above come from it; I did not read the full PDF, so fee treatment and method details are unverified.

candidates.title: NautilusTrader (nautechsystems/nautilus_trader): Rust-core event-driven engine with backtest/live parity and a native Polymarket adapter
candidates.one_line: LGPL-3.0 engine (~30k stars) where the same strategy code runs in deterministic backtest and live; its Polymarket adapter speaks the CLOB directly (limit and market orders, GTC/GTD/FOK, IOC mapped to FAK, post-only, batch submit of 15, L2 deltas, trade states MATCHED -> MINED -> CONFIRMED/FAILED, signature types 0-3) and its docs enumerate live failure modes: overfills, a missing position report is not proof of flat, balances are estimates, and 'do not restart and blindly retry an unknown submission'. Kalshi adapter is listed as planned/beta.
candidates.what_it_adds: Two decisions for Mandel. First, whether the children's execution layer should be this engine rather than hand-rolled asyncio around py-clob-client (now archived; see candidate 9), because a backtest that replays the same event stream the live bot consumes is the precondition for Mandel's held-out-backtest gate to mean anything for an arbitrage strategy. Second, even if not adopted, the Polymarket integration page is the best available checklist of live-trading invariants (asynchronous settlement, reconciliation under lagging replicas, residual dust on close) that Mandel should convert into tests a child must pass before promotion. The project itself warns v2 release candidates are not for production.

candidates.title: Polymarket developer documentation (CLOB, Gamma, Data and WebSocket specs, fees, session keys) with Kalshi's official SDK and API-spec page
candidates.one_line: Machine-readable index of Polymarket's current docs: CLOB OpenAPI (/api-spec/clob-openapi.yaml), Gamma OpenAPI (/api-spec/gamma-openapi.yaml), Data API v2 (https://data-api.polymarket.com/v2/openapi.json), WebSocket AsyncAPI (https://ws-live-v2.polymarket.com/asyncapi.json), fee schedule, wallets/auth, session keys, builder-tier rate limits. Kalshi's equivalent is https://docs.kalshi.com/sdks/overview, which says the REST OpenAPI (https://docs.kalshi.com/openapi.yaml) and WebSocket AsyncAPI (https://docs.kalshi.com/asyncapi.yaml) are the source of truth, SDKs are kalshi_python_sync/async (kalshi-python deprecated), auth is API key plus signed requests (RSA, or Ed25519 from SDK 3.31.0).
candidates.what_it_adds: Ground truth that has moved under the repo and the user's trading videos: Polymarket/py-clob-client (https://github.com/Polymarket/py-clob-client) is archived and says not to use it for new or existing integrations, replaced by the unified SDK https://github.com/Polymarket/py-sdk (0.x, breaking changes allowed); Polymarket/agents (https://github.com/Polymarket/agents) was archived May 2026; the old docs.polymarket.com/developers/CLOB/introduction path is a 404. Mandel should store both exchanges' OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specs as versioned files in its knowledge base, diff them on a schedule, and emit a child-facing change notice when endpoints, fee rates or auth schemes change, rather than learning about breakage from failed orders. The fee page gives the exact p(1-p) taker-fee formula the arbitrage math must include. Official primary documentation, not research.

candidates.title: Metaculus metac-bot-template + forecasting-tools: forecasting bots with publicly scored track records in the AI Benchmarking / FutureEval tournaments
candidates.one_line: A GitHub-Actions bot (tournament workflow every 20 minutes, skips already-forecast questions, dry-run flag) that researches via AskNews and forecasts through an LLM wrapper with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY supported out of the box (forecasting-tools uses litellm; MIT); forecasts are submitted before resolution and scored afterwards against other bots and Metaculus pro forecasters, giving the only widely used class of prediction bot with a public, leakage-free track record.
candidates.what_it_adds: The honest answer to 'prediction-market bot repos with real track records': the open-source Polymarket/Kalshi arbitrage bots I found (https://github.com/realfishsam/prediction-market-arbitrage-bot and its write-up https://dev.to/realfishsam/how-i-built-a-risk-free-arbitrage-bot-for-polymarket-kalshi-4f, https://github.com/CarlosIbCu/polymarket-kalshi-btc-arbitrage-bot, ImMike/polymarket-arbitrage) publish spread claims of 1.5-4.5% but no P&L, fee modeling or trade counts, so none qualifies and Mandel should record them as unverified. Mandel should adopt the Metaculus pattern for its own calibration gate: log every forecast before resolution, score only after, keep a per-child Brier/peer-score ledger, and run a shadow bot in the Metaculus tournament as an external, un-gameable calibration check on whatever forecasting model the children share. Related evaluation design: ForecastBench (https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19839; questions with no known answer at submission) and Halawi et al. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18563; retrieval + aggregation nears the crowd). The Metaculus AIB page itself returned 403 from this container.
